# fullstackgtm

> Plan/apply for your GTM stack: canonical CRM/GTM data model, deterministic
> hygiene audits, reviewable dry-run patch plans, and approval-gated
> write-back to HubSpot and Salesforce; Stripe is read-only. Think
> `terraform plan` for your CRM. Apache-2.0.

CLI quick check: `fullstackgtm doctor --json`. Zero-credential demo:
`fullstackgtm audit --demo --json`. Audits are read-only; `apply` writes only
explicitly approved operation ids. Exit codes: 0 success, 1 error, 2 findings
at/above `--fail-on`.

MCP apply accepts only a stored `planId`; approvals and concrete values come
from the HMAC-signed plan store, never the tool caller. MCP never executes rule
packages or external plans. Store-backed apply is single-owner and journaled;
an interrupted provider attempt remains uncertain and is never auto-replayed.
After reconciling provider state, `plans recover <id>
--acknowledge-uncertain-writes` clears approvals for a fresh human review.

## Docs

- [README](https://github.com/fullstackgtm/core/blob/main/README.md): install, five-minute loop, auth ladder, MCP setup, programmatic use
- [INSTALL_FOR_AGENTS](https://github.com/fullstackgtm/core/blob/main/INSTALL_FOR_AGENTS.md): deterministic install-and-verify steps with expected outputs
- [Agent skill](https://github.com/fullstackgtm/core/blob/main/skills/fullstackgtm/SKILL.md): compact operating guide, installable via `npx skills add fullstackgtm/core`
- [Recipes](https://github.com/fullstackgtm/core/blob/main/docs/recipes.md): five composable GTM plays over the primitives (cold-start lead-fill, the trigger→judge→draft outbound loop, scheduled-continuous, ABM-from-companies, hygiene-gated outbound) — the CLI ships primitives, your agent is the orchestrator, the package never sends
- [Architecture](https://github.com/fullstackgtm/core/blob/main/docs/architecture.md): module map + snapshot → audit → plan → apply data flow; "where do I add a rule/connector/operation"
- [Contributing](https://github.com/fullstackgtm/core/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md): dev setup, the open-core mirror model, the release ritual
- [API reference](https://github.com/fullstackgtm/core/blob/main/docs/api.md): semver-covered surfaces — canonical model, rule interface, plan/apply contract, connector contract, config, CLI, MCP tools
- [CRM-health lifecycle](https://github.com/fullstackgtm/core/blob/main/docs/crm-health-lifecycle.md): the Prevent → Detect → Remediate → Verify/Attribute model; no-new-dupes design
- [TAM mapping](https://github.com/fullstackgtm/core/blob/main/docs/tam.md): size the reachable market from the ICP, then populate it with scheduled governed acquire and track coverage to an ETA
- [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/fullstackgtm/core/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md): release history

`fullstackgtm resolve <type>` is the create gate: exit 0 = safe to create,
exit 2 = exists/ambiguous (never blind-create); duplicate findings carry
"Created by:" writer attribution when the provider exposes record source.

## Key invariants (calls)

`fullstackgtm call parse` defaults to LLM extraction (BYO Anthropic/OpenAI
key; env or stored via `login anthropic|openai`); `--deterministic` is the
free keyword baseline; `call score --rubric` produces evidence-quoted
coaching scorecards; `call link` suggests the deal with confidence + reason;
`call plan` proposes governed next-step writes through the standard
approve/apply lifecycle.

## Key invariants (market map)

`fullstackgtm market` models the competitive category: vendors + claim
taxonomy in `market.config.json`; `capture` stores vendor pages
content-addressed; `classify` (BYO key, same ladder as calls) or
`worksheet` + `observe` (agent/human channel) propose LOUD/QUIET/ABSENT
intensity readings per vendor × claim. Every quoted evidence span is
mechanically verified verbatim against the stored capture it cites;
unverifiable quotes are rejected (`--unverified` only when captures live
elsewhere). Failed captures read UNOBSERVABLE, never ABSENT. `fronts --diff`
= deterministic front states + drift between runs; `axes` = PCA axis
discovery + orthogonality screen; `report` = self-contained HTML field
report; `refresh` = capture → classify → drift → report in one command.
`overlay --snapshot <crm.json> [--calls <files>]` joins observations to YOUR
CRM/calls (deterministic mention matching, no LLM) and emits OCCUPY/PROMOTE/
URGENT/RETREAT directives — each needs ≥1 observation + ≥1 CRM stat with
sample size; below thresholds = no directive; `--save` = approval-gated
create_task ops. `scale` = citable scaleSignals (sourceUrl + verbatim quote
each) → revenue-space estimates calibrated within-set by acvBand, disclosed
uncertainty; report bubbles ∝ estimated share only when signals exist.
Storage is profile-scoped under `<home>/market/<category>`. MCP:
`fullstackgtm_market_worksheet`, `fullstackgtm_market_observe`.

## Key invariants (TAM mapping)

`fullstackgtm tam` sizes the reachable market FROM the ICP and then iteratively
fills it — not a one-shot headline. `tam estimate` computes a transparent model:
account universe × ACV = TAM (account/per-logo basis by default; `--acv-basis
buyer` for per-seat = contacts × ACV), where contacts = accounts ×
buyers/account is the population target. The account count is `--accounts <n>`
(assumption), OR `--source theirstack` — the TECHNOGRAPHIC universe: counts
companies that USE a CRM/MAP (`firmographics.technologies` → TheirStack
`company_technology_slug_or`) + geo + employee bounds; the real RevOps buying signal
AND the only source that returns a LIST (`tam accounts --source theirstack` pulls
real companies name/domain, `--out csv`/`--json`, `--max` caps credit spend; a
count is cheap but NOT free — limit:0 is rejected so a count returns 1 row ≈ 3
credits, a list pull ≈ 3/company; `login theirstack`). OR `--source explorium` — a firmographic
count via `/v1/businesses` (`total_results`), a count ONLY (Explorium 403s on
list-pull, can't target by CRM-usage; must OMIT `size` or it caps the total; capped
at 60,000 `EXPLORIUM_BUSINESS_COUNT_CAP` → `provider:explorium (≥60k cap — floor)` +
⚠). Verified live: people endpoints can't size a market (Explorium `/v1/prospects`
total == page size; pipe0/Crustdata returns only a cursor — `--source pipe0` for
estimate is REJECTED, it's a population source). The model always LABELS
`accountsSource` (provider:theirstack/explorium vs assumption). ACV must be a
real ANNUAL figure the operator CONFIRMS — `--acv <annual-usd>`, OR `--acv-from-crm
--deal-period monthly|quarterly|annual` which takes the median closed-won amount and
ANNUALIZES it (the period is required — a deal can be MRR/quarterly/annual and
guessing is a 4–12× error; $15k/mo → $180k). NO band defaults, and a bare
`--provider` does NOT auto-set ACV (HubSpot is the COVERAGE source, not the ACV) —
`estimate` REFUSES without a confirmed ACV. Buyers/account is `--buyers-per-account`
OR the CRM's avg-contacts-per-account OR a labeled `assumption:1-buyer`. Both
`acv.source` and `universe.buyersSource` are labeled (incl. deal count + the
period×factor, so a thin signal like "1 deal" is visible). Optional
citable cross-checks (`{claim,valueUsd?,sourceUrl,quote}`) sit beside the
bottom-up number as a top-down sanity check. `estimate`
records a coverage BASELINE (CRM counts now) so `status` attributes what the
campaign added. `tam populate --cron` schedules `enrich acquire --source <s>
--save` — the ONE create-side verb the schedule allowlist permits, and only in
its plan-producing `--save` form: each firing queues a needs_approval lead plan,
the acquire meter is charged only at apply, and apply stays `apply --plan-id`
(re-checked approved). `tam status` measures coverage on the INTERSECTION of CRM ×
TAM-ICP, not a raw count: `tam estimate` stores the ICP filter (`model.targeting`),
and status CLASSIFIES each domain-bearing account into in-TAM / out-of-TAM / unknown
(checked on size+industry — geo + "uses-CRM" aren't on a CanonicalAccount, so a
`--reverify` re-enrich is future; the classifier labels what it checked). ONLY
in-TAM counts toward coverage, so off-ICP accounts loaded from elsewhere can't
inflate it. Bottom-up vs top-down reconciliation: the in-TAM count is a FLOOR on the
real universe (those are verified members), so when in-TAM ≥ the estimate, status
stops reporting a fake 100% and flips to "estimate was a floor — real market is at
least N (`reconciledUniverse = max(estimate, inTam)`); re-estimate for the headroom".
`--save` stamps an append-only timeline. `tam report` (markdown) and `status` project
an ETA on the IN-TAM accounts/day burn across the timeline → days-remaining → fill
date — and REFUSE to project (honest "not enough history") below two readings, a flat
rate, or zero elapsed time.
Coverage + ETA are deterministic (no LLM, byte-stable). Storage profile-scoped
under `<home>/tam/<name>/` (`model.json` + `coverage.jsonl`, 0600).

## Key invariants (governed write verbs)

`bulk-update <object> --where … (--set|--archive|--create-task)` filters the
snapshot into a dry-run plan; the FULL filter is re-verified per record at
apply time (plus mid-apply rechecks); equality filters double as
preconditions, `--require`/`--guard` add explicit ones, `--max-operations`
caps blast radius. Filter operators: `=` `!=` `~` `!~` `:empty` `:notempty`,
plus type-aware comparisons `<` `>` `<=` `>=` (`today` resolves to the policy
date, e.g. `closeDate<today`; date fields compare as dates, numeric as
numbers, unset/non-parseable values do not match). For date/count hygiene
(past close dates, stale deals, missing accounts, duplicates) prefer the
rule-backed `fix --rule <id>` — it encodes the date/open-deal logic
deterministically; reach for bulk-update only when no rule covers the task. `--set f=from:<source>` derives per-record values (empty
source = skip + count, never guess). `--archive` refuses records sharing an
identity key — merge with `dedupe` instead. `dedupe <object> --key
<domain|email|name>` = one merge_records op per duplicate group,
deterministic survivor (`--keep richest|oldest`); merges are irreversible and
stay low-confidence-capped at approval. `reassign --from <owner> --to
<owner>` = ownership handoff plans per object type; `--except-deal-stage`
also excludes records whose account has an open deal in that stage;
`reassign --assign-unowned --to <id>` instead claims every ownerless record
(`ownerId:empty`) for an owner — the backfill twin of acquire's create-time
assignment. `fix
--rule <id>` = audit one rule → suggest → approve at the confidence bar →
apply only with `--yes`. All four produce plans; none writes outside
approve → apply.

## Key invariants (enrich)

`fullstackgtm enrich` is governed enrichment: `append` pulls (Apollo, BYO key
via `login apollo`/APOLLO_API_KEY) or reads data staged by `ingest` (Clay CSV
exports / webhook payload JSON), matches source records to CRM records via
ordered keys in `enrich.config.json` (unique hit wins; ambiguity skips or
becomes `requires_human_record_selection` placeholders — never a coin flip),
and emits a fill-blanks-only patch plan through the normal dry-run → approve →
apply gate. No `--save` = dry-run diff, nothing written. `refresh` re-checks
stale fields the run-store ledger proves enrich stamped, proposing ops only
where the source value changed (beforeValue = current CRM value → apply-time
CAS). Conflict policy MVP is `never`; `system-only`/`always` are phase 2 and
refused explicitly. Run store (checkpoint + staleness ledger + `status`) is
profile-scoped under `<home>/enrich/runs`. No cron — scheduling is horizontal.
`acquire` is the one enrich verb that creates net-new records instead of
filling blanks: it discovers ICP-targeted people, resolves work email, and
proposes governed `create_record` ops through the same dry-run → approve →
apply gate — resolve-first dedupe re-checks the key at apply time so it never
double-creates. A per-profile windowed meter (`acquireMeter.ts`) caps both
record count and provider spend (per-day + per-month, whichever binds first);
sources come from staged ingest lists. Acquired leads are never born ownerless:
an `acquire.assign` policy (`fixed`/`round-robin`/`territory`/`account-owner`,
or `--assign-owner <id>`) stamps an owner into every `create_record`, gated by
the snapshot's active owners (unknown/inactive owner → unassigned, never a bad
owner); with multiple owners and no policy it warns and leaves leads unassigned.
Discovery sources are presets behind `--source`: `explorium`/`pipe0` (ICP-driven
people search) and `linkedin` (Phase 1, discovery + dry-run) which reads a
pre-built HeyReach lead list (`--list <id>` or `acquire.discovery.linkedin.listId`,
match key = LinkedIn URL, $0/record, `login heyreach`/`HEYREACH_API_KEY`) via the
injectable `LinkedInProvider` (default HeyReach; `FakeLinkedInProvider` for tests).
LinkedIn is read-only — Phase 1 has no `linkedin_connect`/`linkedin_message` ops
and no webhook ingestion (Phase 2). Never auto-writes.

## Key invariants (GTM brain — signals / icp / judge / draft)

The timing/outbound layer turns "who changed" into one grounded, governed
opener — and **never sends**. `signals fetch` captures fresh buying triggers
into a profile-scoped ledger (free Greenhouse/Lever/Ashby ATS scrapers in the
box; funding/social via `--from`; connected platforms via `--connector`
file/serpapi-news/hubspot-forms with secrets through the credential ladder; and
push platforms via the webhook spool — `--connector file` reads the conventional
landing zone `<home>/signals/spool/*.jsonl`, see docs/signal-spool-format.md),
keyed by **account domain**, ranked by learned `weights`; it writes NOTHING to
the CRM. `signals discover` starts from editable ICP behavioral hypotheses,
searches canonical public ATS evidence through Exa with explicit request and
reported-cost limits, resolves official employer domains, and writes NOTHING
unless `--save` persists the local signal ledger. `icp interview|set|show`
builds `icp.json`; `icp judge` ranks fresh signals into send/nurture/skip — pass
a snapshot (`--provider`/`--input`/`--demo`) and each decision resolves its CRM
target: `accountId`, the best `contact {id,email,title}`, and `contacts[]` (all
in-CRM contacts at the account, titled-first, cap 10, for multi-threading);
`--with-history` additionally gates memory (don't re-touch a recently-touched
account) and fit-scoring. `icp eval` is the calibration gate (exit 2 below the
bar). `draft` emits ONE trigger-grounded opener per hot account as a governed
`create_task` targeting the resolved `contact.id` (or `accountId`) — a
domain-only decision (account not yet in the CRM) is REJECTED with "acquire it
first" (run `enrich acquire`, re-judge with the snapshot). `--channel
email|linkedin|task` shapes the opener. After `plans approve`, applying the draft
plan logs the touch as a CRM task (`apply --provider <crm>`) OR renders it to the
governed outbox (`apply --channel outbox` → `<home>/signals/outbox/<channel>.jsonl`
for a downstream sender to drain). Either way the CLI **transmits nothing** — the
outbox is the send-side mirror of the spool; the always-on sender is hosted/opt-in. `signals outcome --account <domain>
--contact <id> --result replied|...` credits the contact reached so weights
re-learn. The contact↔account join (`contact.accountId` + `account.domain`) is
surfaced at every hop, so the loop is contact-coherent end to end — see the
[recipes](https://github.com/fullstackgtm/core/blob/main/docs/recipes.md).

## Key invariants (schedule)

`fullstackgtm schedule` is the horizontal scheduler — no feature namespace
owns cron logic. `add "<command>" --cron "<expr>"` validates the command
against the read/plan-side allowlist (audit, snapshot, enrich append|refresh,
enrich acquire --save, market capture|refresh, signals fetch|discover, icp judge|eval,
draft, suggest, report, doctor) and the 5-field cron
expression, but touches no system timer; `install` materializes enabled
entries into the platform timer (`--timer` defaults launchd on macOS,
crontab elsewhere). crontab: a sentinel-delimited managed block
(`# >>> fullstackgtm <profile> >>>`) replaced wholesale on re-install, lines
outside it untouched. launchd: one LaunchAgent plist per entry
(`com.fullstackgtm.<profile>.<id>` in `~/Library/LaunchAgents`), the fleet
replaced wholesale, foreign plists untouched — chosen because macOS gates
`crontab` writes behind Full Disk Access (unpromptable TCC), while
LaunchAgents need no permission and coalesce firings missed during sleep
into one run on wake. `uninstall` removes only what install created.
Scheduling never auto-approves: `apply` is
schedulable ONLY as `apply --plan-id <id>` and every firing re-checks the
plan is approved — unapproved plans record a `plan_not_approved` no-op run,
no flag relaxes this. `schedule run <id>` is the single provider entry point
(in-process dispatch, never shell; a second cron trigger in the same minute
records a `duplicate_firing` no-op — launchd double-triggers the Vixie
dom+dow OR corner); run records (exit code, output tail,
artifacts: plan ids / enrich run labels, trigger cron|manual) land under
`<home>/schedule/runs/<id>/`. `status` shows next firing and surfaces missed
firings (visibility only — cron has no catch-up). Providers beyond
`local` are not yet implemented (future: codegen scaffolds, same contract).

## Key invariants (engagement workspace / health)

`fullstackgtm health` rolls up a per-profile CRM-health timeline that accrues
from the verb teams already run: every `audit --save` stamps a deterministic
0–100 hygiene score plus a snapshot onto the active profile. The score is
`100 / (1 + severity-weighted findings per record)` (info ×1, warning ×3,
critical ×10) — no LLM, so it is byte-stable in CI and comparable run-over-run;
0 findings ⇒ 100, and the same findings over fewer clean records score lower.
State is profile-scoped and owner-only (0600) under the same secured home as
plans: `health.jsonl` (append-only, one entry per saved audit) and
`snapshots/<planId>.json`. `health` is READ-ONLY — it only reads the timeline,
never re-audits or writes; `--json` emits the rollup (current score, delta since
the last audit, dated trend, per-rule deltas). Scope per client with
`--profile <name>`; an empty timeline returns a pointer, never an error.
Library: `computeHealth` / `summarizeHealth` / `healthToMarkdown`.

## Key invariants

- Reads are safe by default; nothing is written without explicit `--approve`
- `requires_human_*` placeholder values are refused without a `--value` override
- Finding/operation ids are stable hashes of rule + record (diffable across runs)
- Secrets are never accepted as argv flags; stdin or env only
